content: The enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of many drugs. The following are specific interactions and recommendations for the co-administration of quinupristin/dalfopristin with other medications: 1. Lumateperone: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases lumateperone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 2. Lumequine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases lumequine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Lurbinectedin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin significantly increases lurbinectedin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Maraviroc: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases maraviroc levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Mavacamten: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases mavacamten levels. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. Monitor closely. 6. Mavorixafor: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases mavorixafor levels. Monitor for adverse effects and reduce the mavorixafor dose if necessary. 7. Mestranol: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases mestranol levels but may decrease its effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 8. Methadone: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases methadone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Methylprednisolone: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases methylprednisolone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Microbiota (oral): Quinupristin/dalfopristin decreases the efficacy of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. 11. Midazolam (intranasal): Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases midazolam levels, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Montelukast: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases montelukast levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 13. Naldemedine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases naldemedine levels. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 14. Nelfinavir: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nelfinavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Neratinib: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases neratinib levels. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Nicardipine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nicardipine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Nifedipine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nifedipine levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 18. Nilotinib: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nilotinib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Nimodipine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nimodipine levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 20. Nirogacestat: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nirogacestat levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Nisoldipine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nisoldipine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Nitrendipine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases nitrendipine levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 23. Norgestrel: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases norgestrel levels, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Oliceridine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases oliceridine levels. Adjust dosing frequency and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 25. Omaveloxolone: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases omaveloxolone levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose to 100 mg/day and monitor for adverse effects. 26. Oxybutynin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases oxybutynin levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 27. Paclitaxel: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases paclitaxel levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 28. Pazopanib: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases pazopanib levels. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Pimozide: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases pimozide levels by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Prednisone: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases prednisone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Quetiapine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases quetiapine levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Ranolazine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases ranolazine levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Repaglinide: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases repaglinide levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Ritonavir: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases ritonavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Saxagliptin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases saxagliptin levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 36. Seladelpar: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases seladelpar levels. Use caution, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. 37. Selumetinib: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases selumetinib levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Simvastatin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases simvastatin levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Siponimod: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases siponimod levels. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Sirolimus: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases sirolimus levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Tadalafil: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases tadalafil levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Tazemetostat: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases tazemetostat levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Temsirolimus: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases temsirolimus levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Tezacaftor: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases tezacaftor levels. Adjust the dosage regimen if co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 45. Theophylline: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases theophylline levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Thiamine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin decreases thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. The significance is unknown. 47. Tinidazole: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases tinidazole levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Tolvaptan: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases tolvaptan levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Trazodone: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases trazodone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Triamcinolone: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases triamcinolone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Triazolam: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases triazolam levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Quinupristin/dalfopristin decreases the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering the vaccine. 53. Vardenafil: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases vardenafil levels. Adjust the dose if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Verapamil: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases verapamil levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Vilazodone: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases vilazodone levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Vinblastine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases vinblastine levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 57. Vincristine: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases vincristine levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 58. Voclosporin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases voclosporin levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 59. Zaleplon: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases zaleplon levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 60. Zanubrutinib: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases zanubrutinib levels. Reduce the dose to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 61. Zolpidem: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases zolpidem levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 62. Zonisamide: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases zonisamide levels. The significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Adverse Effects: Common side effects include local pain, inflammation at the infusion site, hyperbilirubinemia, edema, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Serious effects include QTc prolongation, hypersensitivity reactions, and potential for drug-resistant bacteria with inappropriate use. Special Considerations: Avoid prescribing in the absence of a proven bacterial infection. Use caution in hepatic impairment. Pregnancy Category B: No evidence of fetal risk in controlled studies. Lactation: Effects are unknown. Administration: Reconstitute with sterile water or D5W and dilute further for infusion. Avoid freezing the solution and administer over one hour to reduce toxicity risks.
